title: Collapsible Rigid Box Assembly: An MTT Perfume Duo
seoTitle: Collapsible Rigid Box Assembly Checklist | MTT
summary: Plan collapsible rigid box assembly around corner fixing, insert installation and lid fit. Explore MTT’s perfume duo design and a practical sample checklist.
intro: For collapsible rigid box assembly, confirm how the corners lock before installing the insert or loading the product. Review the empty shell, assembled geometry and complete loaded box separately. The MTT perfume duo shown here pairs a blue exterior with an orange interior and two bottle positions. Its flat view helps identify assembly questions; the approved sample must settle the fixing method, sequence and finished fit.
cta: Send your product dimensions, filled weights, quantity and intended packing location. Include the corner-fixing drawing or a sample reference so MTT can review the shell, insert and assembly sequence together.
sections: Read the empty shell before the finished presentation

The flat view exposes the triangular corner panels that disappear beneath the insert in the loaded presentation. Check which panels move, which surfaces meet and where the assembler needs to apply pressure. A magnetic lid closure does not tell you how those corners are secured.

Request a fixing detail identifying any tape, adhesive, slot or other connection. If the chosen design uses a release liner, specify when to remove it and how to keep it away from the interior. Do not assume that a completed box can be flattened repeatedly: permanent corner bonds and reusable locking arrangements need different instructions.

See the MTT perfume duo product views alongside the rigid box options. This article focuses on assembly; the freight planning guide covers the separate shipping-cost decision.
Assemble the shell before using the insert as a brace

1. Place the empty shell on a clean, level surface and orient the lid away from the operator.
  2. Raise the walls in the sequence agreed on the assembly drawing. Keep the wrapping paper clear of trapped corner folds.
  3. Engage the specified corner fixings. Inspect every connection before covering it.
  4. Compare the two diagonals and check the base sits flat. Record the agreed acceptance range on the sample sheet.
  5. Install the insert, then load the two bottles and card.
  6. Close the lid and reopen it to inspect clearance and product removal.

The sequence above is a review framework, not a verified work instruction for a particular adhesive. Stop if the insert is needed to force an out-of-square shell into shape. That can hide a corner or hinge problem until the box is loaded.
Confirm the bond on the actual finished surface

A smooth printed wrap, a coated flap and exposed board present different bonding surfaces. Ask the assembler which surface receives the fixing and whether print, foil or lamination crosses that area. Review pressure and any waiting time against the selected adhesive supplier’s instructions.

Henkel’s paper-converting guidance identifies substrate, coatings, equipment and storage conditions as variables in packaging performance. It supports checking the real combination; it does not supply a universal glue quantity or curing time for this box.

Keep a sample assembled using the intended materials and method. Note lifting corners, exposed adhesive, whitening at folds and wrap delamination. If a component changes, repeat the affected check rather than relying only on the old exterior appearance.
Check the loaded box without compressing the bottles

The orange deck has two bottle positions and a separate card area. Identify the support beneath each bottle; a neat visible opening is only one part of the insert. Confirm the bottle base sits on its intended support and that the card cannot slide into the hinge.

Close the lid with both finished bottles, caps and any tissue in place. If it closes empty but springs up when loaded, investigate the stack height before increasing magnetic strength. Inspect the necks, cap tops and lid lining for contact marks, then remove each bottle using the intended grip.

Keep this fit review separate from transport protection. Evaluate the loaded presentation box inside its specified outer package. Use the sample approval process to record the shell, insert and outer-pack versions together.
Make the packing instruction useful at the receiving site

Record who erects the boxes, where inserts are stored and when the products arrive. If cartons of shells and inserts travel separately, mark their matching references. Keep assembly photographs with the approved sample instead of relying on a verbal explanation.

Assembly approval record
CheckpointRecord
Corner fixingMethod, position and material reference
Shell geometryFinished dimensions and agreed diagonal check
Loaded closureBottle, insert and card versions used
Packing trialOperator, conditions, observed rework and measured time

Measure assembly time during the trial if it affects the sourcing decision. Keep that result tied to the operator and setup; do not turn one trial into a universal output rate. A box that travels flat still needs a workable receiving-site process.

title: Paper Bag Material Comparison for Perfume Retail Packs
seoTitle: Paper Bag Material Comparison: Kraft or Coated? | MTT
summary: Compare kraft and coated paper for a perfume shopping bag. Review print, handle reinforcement, the base and a loaded sample before selecting the material.
intro: A paper bag material comparison should start with the filled retail pack, not a preferred paper weight. Compare kraft and coated paper for appearance, printing and conversion, then review the handle attachment and reinforced base together. The green and coral MTT perfume bag shown here uses ribbon handles and a coordinated printed exterior. The material specification still needs to match the actual box dimensions, loaded weight and carrying conditions.
cta: Share the finished outer box dimensions, total carrying weight, quantity and desired print reference. MTT can review paper options, handles and reinforcement as one bag specification.
sections: Start with the retail carrying job

The pictured bag is a retail carry component. Its broad printed panels and ribbon handles connect it visually to the fragrance inside. It should be sized around the finished boxed product and its insertion orientation, including any pouch, card or tissue.

Distinguish a bag carried briefly from a shop from one expected to hold several heavy products during a longer event. Write down the intended use rather than asking for a universally “strong” paper. A shopping bag is also a different component from the outer carton used to ship the product.

Review the MTT perfume ribbon bag and paper bag purchasing options. Use the paper bag dimensions guide for width, gusset and height; this article addresses the material decision.
Compare the surface against the actual artwork

Material comparison for a retail bag sample
CandidateDecision to reviewPhysical check
Kraft paperWhether the selected shade and surface fit the brand artworkPrint the logo and important colours on that grade
Coated paperPrint detail, finish and fold appearanceReview the finished sheet after printing and conversion
Either optionHandle and base construction for the loadCarry the complete product arrangement using the agreed sample plan

Brown kraft can be an intentional part of the design, but its base colour becomes part of the print result. White kraft is a separate candidate, not merely a colour setting for brown paper. A coated candidate also needs a named grade and surface specification.

The pictured coral shapes and deep green areas are useful places to inspect consistency, folds and visible rubbing. Approve the actual printed bag beside the matching box. A screen image cannot settle the physical colour match.
Paper weight does not specify the complete bag

Grammage describes mass per unit area. It does not identify the fibre furnish, sheet thickness, direction-dependent properties, coating or converted bag construction. Keep the supplier’s named grade and relevant technical data with the sample.

Holmen’s technical information lists grammage, thickness and mechanical properties separately for paperboard. That distinction is useful when reading specifications, but its paperboard grades are not bag load ratings. Request data for the actual bag paper instead of copying a board specification into the order.

Use the GSM and thickness guide to distinguish those measurements. If a heavier candidate also changes the fold or handle area, assess the converted result. Increasing one number does not approve the finished bag.
Follow the load from the handle to the base

Start at the coral ribbon handles. Confirm the attachment method, how the top fold is reinforced and which area transfers the load into the bag wall. Pulling on an empty handle does not represent carrying the assembled fragrance set.

Then inspect the bottom fold and reinforcement. A rigid perfume box may concentrate load along its edges; confirm how it rests on the base and whether the corners catch during insertion. Review the seam and handle locations with the actual product arrangement.

Agree a loaded sample check covering the intended carrying movement and duration. Record the full weight, paper grade, handle specification and observed damage. There is no justified kilogram capacity to publish from these pictures alone.
Check finishing and assembly as a combination

The catalogue specification describes a coated shopping-bag paper with gloss lamination and colour printing. Review the assembled top fold, panel edges and bottom after finishing. Ask how the chosen coating or film affects the adhesive area and whether reinforcement changes the feel at the handle.

Henkel describes coatings, substrates and converting conditions as interacting variables. The practical purchasing step is to sample the actual paper, finish and bonding method together. Do not approve an unprinted paper swatch as though it were the completed bag.

Where end-of-life requirements matter, specify the whole construction, including film, ribbon and reinforcement. Ask the intended collection or processing route how that combination is handled; the word “paper” alone does not establish recyclability.
Approve one complete bag specification

Keep the approved print reference, paper grade, finish, handle attachment, reinforcement and finished dimensions under one revision. Confirm whether tissue or a pouch is supplied with the bag or packed separately. Record the loaded sample used for approval.

When comparing quotations, ask each supplier to price the same construction. Otherwise a lower number may reflect a different finish or reinforcement arrangement. If a substitution is proposed, review the affected print, bond and loaded checks before accepting it.

The sampling guide explains how to keep the physical reference and written specification aligned. Choose the bag by the finished retail use, then retain the evidence for reorders.
